author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Export EmuCoreX per-game profiles before a tuning session
summary: Use the Per-Game Settings Manager's JSON export as a versioned snapshot, verify which profiles it contains, tune one title, and understand that importing a snapshot replaces the complete profile collection.
heroAlt: Official EmuCoreX PerGameSettingsManagerScreen source showing the repository-backed profile manager

blocks.text: Understand exactly what the profile export contains

EmuCoreX stores game-specific overrides separately from global defaults. The Per-Game Settings Manager exposes Graphics, System, Controls, and Fixes sections and can export the current collection to emucorex-game-settings.json. The repository writes a profiles array containing the saved entries. It does not turn memory cards, save states, BIOS files, personal disc images, texture packs, or the complete emulator-data folder into a backup.

Import is a collection-level restore, not a merge. The current EmuCoreX repository reads the profiles array from the selected JSON file and writes that list as the complete profile store. Profiles created after the snapshot can therefore disappear after import.
Take a named snapshot before touching the target game

items: 1. Open the Per-Game Settings Manager and allow its game/profile list to finish loading.
2. Select the game you intend to tune and note its title, serial, active-profile badge, renderer, internal resolution, GPU-driver choice, control layout, and any manual fixes.
3. Open the manager's overflow menu and choose Export. Save the proposed emucorex-game-settings.json through Android's document picker.
4. Rename the exported copy outside EmuCoreX with an ISO-style date and purpose, for example 2026-08-09-before-renderer-test.json. Keep the .json extension.
5. Copy that snapshot to a second user-controlled location. Do not store both copies in a temporary downloads or messaging-app cache.
6. Open one copy in a plain-text viewer and confirm that it begins with a JSON object containing a profiles array. Do not edit the verification copy.
7. Search inside the array for the selected game's title or serial and record the total number of profile objects. This count becomes the restore check.

blocks.text: The JSON can contain game keys and configuration choices that reveal storage organization or device-specific tuning. Treat it as private configuration data: remove it from screenshots and support attachments unless the file has been reviewed and redacted. A profile export is small enough to keep several dated generations, so there is no reason to overwrite the last known-good snapshot.

items: Choose a repeatable scene that demonstrates the reason for tuning, then cold-start it with the saved profile before making changes.
Change one control in one manager tab. Renderer, upscale, custom driver, controls, and manual fixes are separate experiments.
Return to the game and repeat the same scene twice. Record correctness, emulation speed, frame pacing, audio, and device temperature as applicable.
Reopen the manager and confirm that only the intended field differs from the pre-test note.
Full-boot a second title that relies on global defaults. Its behavior should not change because the test belongs to one per-game profile.

blocks.text: Choose the narrow rollback before importing everything

If only the selected game is wrong and you know the old value, restore that field in its profile or use the manager's reset action for that game. This preserves newer profiles created elsewhere. Use the JSON import only when the snapshot's complete collection is the state you deliberately want to restore. Before import, export the current collection to a separately named after-test file so nothing is silently lost.
Restore the complete snapshot when that is intentional

items: 1. Export the current collection, label it clearly as the pre-import state, and verify its profiles array.
2. In the Per-Game Settings Manager overflow menu, choose Import and select the untouched dated snapshot.
3. Wait for the success message and for the manager to refresh its list. Do not close Android's picker or EmuCoreX while the file is being read.
4. Compare the visible profile count with the count recorded from the snapshot. A profile-only game may remain listed even when its image is not currently in the library.
5. Open the target profile and verify the saved renderer, resolution, driver selection, controls, and fixes against the pre-test note.
6. Cold-start the target title and one unaffected title. Confirm that the target baseline returned and the global-default title still uses global settings.

blocks.text: Reject a snapshot that fails basic integrity checks

items: The file is empty, truncated, or does not contain a top-level profiles array.
The profile count is unexpectedly zero even though the manager showed active profiles at export time.
The file was manually edited by an application that changed quotes, encoding, or JSON structure.
The snapshot came from an unknown person or untrusted download; profiles can contain paths and aggressive game-specific settings.
The snapshot is older than profiles you need and no separate current export exists.

blocks.text: Recover from an unintended collection replacement

Do not create new profiles immediately. Import the pre-import snapshot made at the start of the restore attempt, then compare its profile count and reopen the games that disappeared. If that file was not created, use the newest verified dated export; resetting all profiles cannot reconstruct custom values. Memory cards and in-game saves should remain untouched because the profile repository is separate, so do not overwrite emulator data while repairing only this configuration store.

Retain a stable baseline, a snapshot before major app or Android changes, and a recent working export. Record the EmuCoreX build, phone SoC/GPU, Android build, and purpose beside each file. Periodically test that the oldest retained snapshot opens as JSON and contains the expected array. A backup becomes trustworthy only after its restore scope and replacement behavior are understood.
